PHASE 1 RCA (2026-08-15)

Proven mechanism: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` sends the same `not integration and not external` default selection through Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13. Nineteen audited nodes inspect only immutable repository text/AST, so their assertions are redundantly executed four times even though OS/Python cannot change their input or expected result. The exact nodes are pinned in this ticket.

Discriminating evidence: latest successful Gerrit Verify run 31892203411 took 31m59s; macOS default was 1,545.29s and integration 155.01s, with no individual macOS test over 30s. The exact 19-node set passed locally under `-n 3` in 8.28s. Mixed-module inspection rejected whole-file routing: the same files contain runtime/subprocess contracts that can expose macOS-only defects. Workflow inspection rejected a new Ubuntu shard: it would repeat checkout/install/collection/session setup and consume another runner. Keeping the nodes in the already-running Ubuntu 3.13 cell adds zero runner or fixture cost.

Alternatives ruled out: blanket macOS reduction violates the platform-compatibility contract and closed ticket ropeable-hydrated-siskin; extra sharding violates coercive-paediatric-bug and the operator constraint. Five active OSS projects (pytest, pip, Pydantic, Click, uv) retain behavioral suites on macOS while routing static/lint policy to Linux, so the narrow singleton route meets the standing consensus bar.

Defect legitimacy: defect against the explicit no-redundant-runner-use requirement, limited to invariant policy duplication. General macOS behavioral duplication is intended coverage and remains unchanged. Expected benefit is modest: about 8 seconds macOS / 24.84 aggregate runner-seconds in the measured local environment, not a standalone fix for a 32-minute run. Plan review PASS; Phase 2 may begin.

RED ORACLE / CONTRACT CARD

authoritative_contract: The 19 inventoried OS/Python-invariant repository-policy assertions execute exactly once in the existing Ubuntu 3.13 default-suite process; all unmarked behavior in the seven mixed modules retains its original default selection; no new job or pytest session is added. Authority: this ticket ACs plus `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` platform-compatibility comments.
trigger_preconditions: The shared workflow expands to Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 plus macOS 3.13 and currently gives every cell the same default selector.
production_path: Parse the real reusable workflow and drive real `pytest --collect-only -m` against the seven mixed modules.
test_tier: In-process workflow contract test; a source grep is insufficient because pytest marks may arrive from decorators, module pytestmark, or conftest hooks.
observable_postcondition: The repo_policy collection equals the exact 19-node set; it is disjoint from the non-policy selection; their union equals the original default selection; the primary cell receives the base selector; the other three cells receive `and not repo_policy`; the workflow still has exactly lint/pip-audit/test jobs and exactly two pytest sessions in the test job; integration remains `pytest -m integration`.
negative_control: Every unmarked case in the seven mixed modules remains in the non-policy selection.
ci_gate: `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q`.

Final-form RED observed before any fix: both held-out tests failed (2 failed in 1.68s). The collection oracle found zero repo_policy nodes versus the required 19, and the routing oracle found no matrix-derived repo_policy selector in the default step. Failures are on the intended missing marker/routing postconditions, not import or fixture errors.

## Context
Gerrit Verify run 31892203411 completed in 31m59s; macOS remained the critical path, with the default pytest step taking 1,545.29s and integration 155.01s. The shared `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` runs the same default selector in Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13 for both the Gerrit Verified lane and the `test.yml` branch/PR lane, even for tests whose only input is the immutable checked-out repository tree. A node-level audit identified the exact 19 repository-policy/AST cases below. They passed locally under three workers in 8.28s: an expected macOS reduction of about 8 seconds (0.54% of the sampled 1,545.29s default step) and about 24.84 aggregate runner-seconds removed across the three duplicate cells in the same local environment. This is modest critical-path and runner-contention hygiene, not a standalone cure for a 32-minute run.

Moving whole files or general behavioral tests would weaken macOS platform coverage; adding a new Ubuntu shard would duplicate checkout, install, collection, and session fixtures and consume another contentious runner. Five surveyed active OSS projects (pytest, pip, Pydantic, Click, uv) keep behavioral suites on macOS and run static/lint checks on Linux. Internal precedents feathered-ironclad-macaque and isleless-catatonic-ekaltadeta accept singleton routing; ropeable-hydrated-siskin and coercive-paediatric-bug reject reduced macOS behavioral coverage and extra runner sharding.

## Plan
- Register a strict `repo_policy` pytest marker for tests whose complete contract is an OS/Python-invariant scan of repository text or AST.
- Mark exactly the inventory above at node/function level, not whole mixed modules. Retain runtime, subprocess, filesystem, locking, timeout, and Git behavior in all four cells.
